comment: The factory obligations register (0.9.0) — every forward-looking debt this release carries, in ONE machine-read home, read by scripts/check-obligations.mjs (clockless in lint.yml's machinery block; --clockful ONLY in hygiene.yml's scheduled job). The release's obligations previously lived in three unjoined sources — the ramp fleet (rampNote sites + template/migrations.json records), template/base/tools/deferrals.json, and prose — and gates-catalog.md's docs-sync section recorded the factory-side reader debt this register discharges.

Row schema: { id, kind: release|calendar|condition, target (x.y.z for release; YYYY-MM-DD for calendar; null for condition), sites?: [{file, mustContain?}] (prose anchors, ONE-WAY — the register is the index, the sites are anchors; the both-ways closure is the consumer scan's grammar and was the vacuous-port trap factory-side), reason (>= 40 chars), reviewedOn (YYYY-MM-DD), evidence (URL or repo file ref — REQUIRED for kind:condition) }.

Kinds: release reds CLOCKLESSLY when package.json reaches the target (check-ramp-ledger.mjs's version authority); calendar is judged ONLY under --clockful in the scheduled lane (a verdict that changes with the date must never red a PR); condition NEVER reds on time — shape + evidence is its bar, and discharging one is DELETING it in a reviewed diff.

Unions the reader closes: every template/base/tools/deferrals.json entry id has a condition-or-release row here under the same id (the census); every shipped rampNote site whose `until` is still in the future has a kind:release row targeting its expiry version (the debt the next migrations record will owe, written down before it is due).

DELIBERATELY NOT LEDGERED: .harness/pending/source-fixes.json — it is CONSUMER-side, parked by `update` on the install and self-clearing via the probes in template/migrations.json seededSourceFixes (owned there, checked by scripts/check-seeded-migrations.mjs); a factory row would be a second, staler copy of a record that already has an owner.

obligations.reason: ASD opened consultation on 2026-06-15 to replace the Essential Eight with an ISM-grounded 'Essentials' series (Essentials for enterprise IT first), citing the cloud gap explicitly; reported at roughly 12 months to deprecation and 24 to retirement. Everything built against the E8 in 0.9.9 therefore has a bounded shelf life, and the stated reason for the change IS the product-versus-organisation mismatch tools/essential-eight.json documents. Judged in the scheduled lane only: a verdict that changes with the date must never red a PR. On arrival, re-verify against ASD and either re-date this row or retarget the register at the successor framework.

Essential Eight MFA-11, MFA-12 and MFA-14 require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication at ML3, and the platform cannot supply it today. TOTP is not phishing-resistant. Supabase WebAuthn MFA does produce aal2 (GoTrue IsAAL2Claim accepts mfa/webauthn) but is undocumented, absent from the Dashboard, marked @experimental in auth-js, challengeAndVerify is TOTP-only, and it is a billable add-on the CLI silently downgrades to false when cost is not confirmed. Passkeys are a SEPARATE aal1 primary sign-in system and do not satisfy it. This is a platform ceiling, not a schedule: it discharges when WebAuthn MFA ships documented and dashboard-reachable, by deleting this row and regrading the three requirements together.

MFA-01/04/06 ask that multi-factor authentication IS USED, and after 1.0.0 the only missing ingredient is compulsion: the aal2 rail enforces the second factor for every ENROLLED user on every surface, and the 1.0.0 enrolment surface (the offered TOTP step in both sign-ups, the challenge screens, the security page and screen, the shared mfa-flow ceremony) lets any user enrol end to end — but GoTrue carries no `required` field, so enrolment stays an offer and a user who declines authenticates with one factor. Condition rather than dated because the discharge is a design decision with two shapes, neither of which the harness may default: adopt an upstream mandatory-enrolment control if GoTrue ever ships one, or impose an application-level wall (refuse session bootstrap without a verified factor) — a posture that locks every casual project out of its own scaffold, so it belongs to the consumer, stated here rather than defaulted. The three rows stay not-implemented until one of those lands.

Essential Eight RB-03/RB-05/RB-06/RB-09 concern where backups live and who can reach them. 0.9.9 recorded what the vendor ATTESTS, labelled as attestation rather than as anything this system demonstrates: backups are AES-256 encrypted at rest with keys protected by FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs, stored in S3 on infrastructure independent of the project's own resources. That is a contractual statement in the data processing agreement, not an artefact any control here reads, so it cannot raise a grade. Two things remain unpublished and are recorded as unknowns rather than assumed either way: no storage region for backups is stated, and whether daily backups aging past the plan window (7 / 14 / 30 days) are DELETED or merely made inaccessible is never said — every statement takes the form "can access the last N days", which is an access claim and not a deletion one. RB-05/06/09 stay graded as they were, because "no client role can reach a backup" is true here only because this tree produces no backups of its own: vacuous truth, and the register's own rule is that absence of a surface is never a control. Discharge is a self-produced off-platform backup with its own store and IAM policy, which is an operator decision about where the boundary sits rather than a build to schedule. CONVERTED release/0.10.0 -> condition in 0.10.0, and the conversion is deliberately the HEAVIER bill: a condition row needs `evidence`, but check-obligations.mjs accepts any URL unresolved and any repo path that merely exists, so this row also carries a sites[] anchor byte-checking the exact ceiling sentence in design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md — which the dated row never had to pay. NO OUTCOME CHANGES: every requirement naming this row stays not-implemented. What was false was the DATE, which asserted somebody could schedule the work.

sites.mustContain: CEILING (RB-03/05/06/09): the current grade rests on vacuous truth

obligations.reason: Essential Eight RB-11 requires backup administrator accounts to be prevented from modifying and deleting backups during the retention period. 0.9.9 re-verified the platform surface and the finding got SHARPER AND WEAKER AT THE SAME TIME, which is the point. Sharper: no Delete or Modify action for a backup appears anywhere — not as a row in the published permissions table, and not as any method across all 115 API paths. Weaker: that is an ABSENCE OF SURFACE, not a published control. Supabase nowhere states that backups cannot be deleted; it simply never offers the verb, and no page publishes an immutability, WORM or object-lock guarantee for the buckets holding them (searched: the backups guide, product security, the SOC 2 and HIPAA pages, the shared-responsibility model, the PITR usage page). Reading an unoffered verb as prevention would be exactly the inflation this register exists to refuse. There is also no backup-administrator role to separate: the four published roles are Owner, Administrator, Developer and Read-Only, the table grants backups only View/Download/Restore and PITR only View/Restore, `Developer` holds Download and Restore while being described as unable to change project settings, and `Read-Only` — the only role narrow enough to resemble a custodian — is denied both and is gated behind Team or Enterprise. ONE GAP IS EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIABLE AND MUST NOT BE GRADED IN EITHER DIRECTION: whether reducing the PITR recovery retention period, or removing the PITR add-on, destroys backup data already inside the previous window. The vendor documents the billing consequence and says the period can be changed, and publishes no data-lifecycle statement at all — which is the most plausible undocumented route by which a privileged account could destroy backups during their retention period, and precisely what this requirement asks about. Reachable only for self-produced off-platform dumps under S3 Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode, which binds every principal including the account root. CONVERTED release/0.10.0 -> condition in 0.10.0, and the conversion is deliberately the HEAVIER bill: a condition row needs `evidence`, but check-obligations.mjs accepts any URL unresolved and any repo path that merely exists, so this row also carries a sites[] anchor byte-checking the exact ceiling sentence in design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md — which the dated row never had to pay. NO OUTCOME CHANGES: every requirement naming this row stays not-implemented. What was false was the DATE, which asserted somebody could schedule the work.

sites.mustContain: CEILING (RB-11): an unoffered verb is not a control

obligations.reason: The standing ask-the-CLI config census is blocked UPSTREAM, not on scheduling: no Supabase CLI subcommand parses config.toml without side effects (config push needs a project ref, functions list needs a token, status binds to whichever stack holds the default ports and prints SECRET_KEY/JWT_SECRET). RE-CHECKED at the 0.10.0 arrival (2026-08-13) against the first real pin bump the standing rule has met — the catalog's `supabase: ^2.34.3` range now resolves to 2.114.0 (GA 2026-08-12) rather than the 2.113.0 both prior re-checks read. The CLI became a pnpm/nx monorepo and the Go CLI moved to apps/cli-go, but apps/cli-go/cmd/config.go AT TAG v2.114.0 still registers `push` alone, and supabase/cli#5894 is still open with no milestone and no linked PR. The consumer deferral entry carries the full re-check record and the standing per-arrival rule; this row is its census twin — it discharges only when the side-effect-free subcommand actually ships, by deleting both together. RE-CHECKED AT THE 1.0.0 CUT (2026-08-16), the settlement release that skips 0.12.0 entirely (every comparison is >=, so the 0.12.0 date arrives at this hop): supabase/cli#5894 is still OPEN, still no milestone, still zero comments, and its only cross-references are this harness's own PRs — the upstream condition is unmet, and npm latest is still 2.114.0, so no pin-bump clause fired. The standing rule moves the date ONE RELEASE (reworded from 'one minor' at 1.0.0: the lineage now cuts by release, and 1.1.0 is the next one) across every listed site.

THE DATED FACTS THIS HARNESS DEPENDS ON MOST HAVE NO SCHEDULED FRESHNESS CONTROL, and this row is the standing re-verification obligation that stands in for one. RE-VERIFIED AT 1.0.0 (2026-08-15) against Claude Code 2.1.232 / SDK 0.3.232, by the file's own method rather than by reading: the payload probe re-armed in .claude/settings.local.json (Facts 1/2/3 re-observed — SubagentStop's 14-key payload is key-for-key identical, last_assistant_message untruncated, verdict on the last non-empty line), the torn-hook exit-code matrix re-probed empirically (Fact 12 — identical: every load failure exits 1/fail-open, malformed stdin on an intact hook exits 2), the advisory surface re-queried (Fact 10 — same 28 advisories, floor unchanged at 2.1.163, checkedOn moved), the CI-spawn grep re-run (Fact 5 — still zero), and the hook environment re-captured (Fact 6 — two ADDITIVE deltas: CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET/TOKEN now reach hooks, the token is credential-shaped; CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 again observed in a MAIN session, re-confirming that a depth-cap control keyed on it would brick reviewer spawns). Fact 4's Stop-side payload was re-captured at the following turn end (key-for-key identical, stop_hook_active false, no agent_* fields); NOT RE-RUN: the one-shot stop_hook_active=true transition (it requires deliberately blocking a turn — the 2026-08-07 observation stands, at the original version, and the file says so in place); Facts 7/8/9/11/13 are documentation-sourced and were re-read, not probed. WHY THE ROW SURVIVES ITS OWN DISCHARGE CLAUSE: deleting it on a completed re-probe would recreate the no-freshness-control defect it names the next time Claude Code moves — the honest shape is a RECURRING re-verification row (the auth-posture-cli-census precedent), re-dated at each pass, whose first sites[] anchor pins the CURRENT re-verification date so the next re-observation must move this row in the same diff. A scheduled prober stays refused while Fact 5 holds: a prober needs a live Claude Code session in CI, and 'no CI lane spawns Claude' is a deliberate posture, not an accident to fix.

NARROWED AT 1.0.0 from e2ee-declared-ports-unimplemented, and the narrowing is the discharge of everything that row held except this. The three ports that row anchored as declarations are IMPLEMENTED with zero new dependencies: RecipientWrapPort as X25519 ECIES over WebCrypto's Secure Curves (fresh ephemeral per wrap, HKDF over shared ‖ eph_pk ‖ recipient_pk, AAD role 0x02 binding both points, RFC 7748 vectors against the real engine, a committed known-answer wire); RecoveryPort as a GENERATED 32-byte shown-once recovery code (Crockford base32, the invitations.token_digest custody precedent) with plain HKDF — full-entropy input needs no memory-hard KDF — and AAD role 0x03; DeviceSyncPort as an envelope over HKDF(channelKey) with AAD role 0x04, the pairing ceremony left to the consumer. The keyring ships rewrapItemKey, so rotation is a one-column rewrite and only its orchestration stays consumer-owned; the byte-shaped KeystoreAdapter is KEPT for a reason that is now decisive rather than historical — a non-extractable CryptoKey handle could never feed escrow or device export. WHAT SURVIVES, and why it is a condition rather than a date: a human-CHOSEN passphrase has guessable entropy and would demand Argon2id (RFC 9106); WebCrypto ships no Argon2, and shipping PBKDF2 while calling it 'the KDF' would be the dishonest default the original refusal named. A passphrase-derived escrow is therefore a documented consumer decision priced like the mobile provider — @noble/hashes or a native argon2 — and this row anchors that refusal to the code comment and the README sentence that state it, so a future default cannot land without the register moving. The upstream condition is a WebCrypto Argon2 primitive (none proposed as of 2026-08-16).

The architecture-reviewer's trigger (0.9.5) is scoped to packages/** plus the two structural registers, deliberately NOT apps/** — the triggers file's own doctrine is narrowness first, because an over-matching trigger makes every diff owe every reviewer and gets routed around. Condition: widen to apps/*/lib/** (the web seam files) only once a release of reviewer-ledger evidence shows the packages-scoped trigger earns its verdicts rather than producing noise; the evidence is the .harness/reviewer-ledger.jsonl population at the widening review. RE-REVIEWED FOR 1.0.0, DELIBERATELY AND NOT AS A DATE BUMP: the widening's evidence bar is a release of reviewer-ledger population, and the population available to this review is ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION from where the factory sits — no consumer install's .harness/reviewer-ledger.jsonl reaches this repository, and the factory's own scaffolds never spawn reviewers (no CI lane spawns Claude; the deliberate posture CONTROL-PLANE-FACTS Fact 5 records). So the review RECORDS the refusal rather than the widening, on the trigger file's own narrowness-first doctrine: widening on zero evidence would be exactly the over-match the doctrine exists to refuse, and a stability release does not get to convert an evidence-gated condition into a leap. The row stays until a consumer-reported or maintainer-dogfooded ledger population exists to judge; the condition is unchanged, so the anchor and the trigger scope are byte-identical to 0.9.5.

The full Stop chain executes off-Linux nowhere: the blocker is the DATABASE, not the shell — rls-isolation needs the live Supabase stack (Docker), which the Windows/macOS runners do not carry, while the gate/hook LOGIC is already proven cross-platform by the Windows unit matrix. Condition: discharge needs a supported off-Linux local-stack story upstream, re-checked at every Supabase CLI pin bump, not a date this repo can set.

Supabase Data API grants stop being automatic for projects created on or after this date (three roles including service_role, SEQUENCES revoked too, failure is SQLSTATE 42501 not a silent 404, and the auto_expose_new_tables restore flag is removed the SAME day). The closure SHIPPED in 0.6.0 inside schema-rls; this row is the dated re-verification that the shipped closure and its prose still describe the regime as it actually lands.

Google Play's target API deadline (36 general, 35 Wear/Automotive, 34 TV/XR; two requirement families — submission and continued-distribution). The regime was CUT as already satisfied and not derivable (the form factor is not expressible in this template's config surface); this row is the dated re-verification that the cut still holds at the deadline, re-opening only if the template ever seeds a Wear/Automotive/TV/XR target. PRE-VERIFIED 2026-08-13 in the 0.10.0 release pass, and the DATE IS DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED: the row's job is to ask the question ON the deadline, so slipping it forward would retire the check rather than satisfy it, and a calendar row cannot red a PR in any case (obligations.mjs gates the calendar branch on `clockful`). What the pre-verification found, all local because the claim is local: tools/store-policy.json's androidTargetSdk floor is 36, matching the requirement that takes effect on the target date; expoSdkDefaults maps SDK 57 to targetSdkVersion 36, so a stock scaffold satisfies it without declaring anything; and a search of the seeded config surface for wear/automotive/androidtv/leanback/xr found NO form-factor target — the only occurrences anywhere are store-policy.json's own prose describing the lower floors those form factors would use. The cut therefore still holds, and the scheduled lane's firing on the date is a confirmation rather than a discovery.

CRA Article 14 reporting applies from this date (Art. 71(2); a SINGLE reporting end-point simultaneously accessible to ENISA, not three recipients). This repository is out of scope as unmonetised FOSS — the deliverable was consumer ENABLEMENT (SECURITY.md ships, planted for existing installs) — and this row is the dated re-verification of that scope reading against the final guidance in force on the day. PRE-VERIFIED 2026-08-13 in the 0.10.0 release pass, and the DATE IS DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED, for the same reason as the Play row: 'the guidance in force on the day' is not readable before the day, so moving the target would convert a dated check into a retired one. The local half of the scope reading was re-confirmed — SECURITY.md ships in template/base and is planted for existing installs, so the consumer-enablement deliverable stands whatever the final guidance says about this repository's own status. The row stays undischarged on purpose: it is the one obligation in this register whose answer this repository cannot compute, only look up.

The CRA rows of tools/conformance-map.json carry a SHELF LIFE, and this row is its clock: as of 2026-08-16 NO harmonised standard for Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 had been cited in the Official Journal — ETSI's CRA ENs (the EN 18031-series successors and the horizontal/vertical drafts under standardisation request M/606) were in approval, not cited — so every Annex I disposition in the map is written against the Regulation's own text and the register says so in its header, in the README paragraph, and in the generated crosswalk and threat model. When a harmonised standard IS cited, the map's dispositions acquire a presumption-of-conformity vocabulary they must NOT borrow before the citation exists, and its rows should be re-read against the cited EN's clause structure. Re-verify on 2026-12-31 (and at each cut before that): the OJ citation list for the CRA, the ETSI work-item status, and whether the map's CRA rows still describe the operative text. This is a re-verification date, not a deadline to build anything — a calendar row rides the clockful lane and never reds a PR.

EU AI Act Article 50 transparency: in force since 2026-08-02 with a 2026-12-02 transitional. The recorded disposition is a CONFIRMED NEGATIVE on the role split (Art. 50(2) binds the provider of the generative system, not the author of software written with one); this row is the dated re-verification of that negative when the transitional window closes, since the robust rationale must survive whatever guidance accretes by then.

The COLD path (fresh clone, cold caches, first validate) is unmeasured — the committed measurements cover the warm chain and the Stop turn-end only — so no cold figure may be published, and the README says so. Condition, not a date: the discharge is a reviewed cold-run recording through the same `check-chain-budget --record` channel, which exists only when a runner and a reviewed dispatch produce one.

sites.mustContain: AGENTS.md gate-list lockstep after an injected chain step

obligations.reason: The AGENTS.md gate-list ramp is RE-OPENED at 1.0.0 (minVersion 1.0.0, until 1.1.0) for the third time on the same site, because 1.0.0 injects two chain steps and every existing install's seeded AGENTS.md documents 34 (or fewer) while its chain now runs 36 — the reviewed rampExtensions entry in the 1.0.0 migrations record moves the deadline from 0.9.0 to 1.1.0 and the ramp opens ABOVE the population it protects this time (the 0.11.1 lesson). This row is the expiry's owner: at 1.1.0 the site's `until` arrives, the escape closes for every install below 1.0.0, and the 1.1.0 migrations record owes the rampExpiry entry naming that population (every vintage 0.1.3 through 0.11.1). The upgrade lane's sweep leg performs the paste the NOTE describes (§3 AGENTS.md rewrite) and requires graduate to succeed, so the runbook is proven sufficient before the deadline lands. Discharge = the 1.1.0 record's rampExpiry carrying this site's population, then delete this row.

sites.mustContain: the arrival of tools/eol.json's removalTarget dates

obligations.reason: RE-OPENED A SECOND TIME, at 1.0.0, and the recurrence is now the point of the row. 0.11.1 re-opened this ramp because the escape excluded the one vintage holding the arrived date; 1.0.0 re-opens it because the SAME shape recurred one release on — the 0.11.x vintages hold a seeded tools/eol.json saying 0.12.0, 0.12.0 was never cut, the date arrives at 1.0.0 (>=), and upgrade-lane leg A found it exactly as the 0.11.0 tag's lane found the first. The 1.0.0 record's rampExtensions entry moves (0.11.0, 0.12.0) → (1.0.0, 1.1.0), and the same record's seededSourceFixes probe (contains '"removalTarget": "0.12.0"') delivers the harness's own re-affirmation as a parked fix. THE STANDING RULE, written so it stops being rediscovered: every release that moves the template's uuid removalTarget owes BOTH the seededSourceFixes probe on the old literal (scripts/check-eol-target.mjs demands it) AND an arrival ramp opened at that release's own minVersion, until the next; the ramp's expiry is owed by the next record. Discharge = the 1.1.0 record's rampExpiry naming this site's population (0.11.0 and 0.11.1, plus every older vintage that meets it), OR the upstream discharge (an xcode major off uuid 7 reached by @expo/config-plugins), which retires the row and the ramp together.

sites.mustContain: the inline-suppression census over the product tree

obligations.reason: 1.0.0 injects the `suppressions` chain step (the inline-directive census — the scanner outside ESLint that polices the rule-less disable no in-ESLint check can see) and, per the ramp doctrine, ships its findings NOTE-only for pre-1.0.0 installs until 1.1.0: an install whose seeded tree predates the census must get one release of dated NOTEs to reason each site and adopt the planted tools/suppressions-allow.json register, not a hard red on the update that delivered the scanner. The escape ends at 1.1.0 and the 1.1.0 migrations record owes this expiry. The register is planted (DELIBERATE_PLANT — green-by-construction: its shipped rows describe the harness-seeded files), so the only surviving NOTE source on an upgraded install is a directive ITS OWN tree added without a row, which is exactly the population the census exists to make visible.

1.0.0 injects the `resilience` chain step (the outbound-seam posture register, closed both ways with symbol-backed claims) and ships its findings NOTE-only for pre-1.0.0 installs until 1.1.0, for the same reason as the suppressions ramp one row up: an install that grew its own outbound seams before the scanner existed gets one release of dated NOTEs to declare each seam in the planted tools/resilience.json, never a hard red on the update that delivered the demand. The escape ends at 1.1.0 and the 1.1.0 migrations record owes this expiry. The planted register declares the scaffold's own eight seams, so an upgraded install NOTEs only on transports its own tree constructed — the undeclared-posture population the register exists to close over.

sites.mustContain: the behavior-keyed widening of the vertical-anatomy DAL laws

obligations.reason: 1.0.0 re-keys the vertical-anatomy DAL laws on BEHAVIOR — a value-import of @app/supabase/@supabase reds anywhere under src/**, and a file that speaks PostgREST (.from(/.rpc(/.select( in call position) must import a port.ts that exists, wherever both live — discharging vertical-anatomy-folder-name-coupling (the src/repo/ service-role escape the directory keying admitted by construction). Per the ramp doctrine the WIDENED findings ship NOTE-only for pre-1.0.0 installs until 1.1.0: a vertical that satisfied the 0.9.5 directory keying (its DAL under src/data/ with a port beside it) may hold a PostgREST caller elsewhere that never owed a port import before, and it gets one release of dated NOTEs to route the seam through a port or record the reviewed allow entry, never a hard red on the update that delivered the re-keying. Nothing weakens meanwhile: findings the directory keying already produced keep their vintage tag and stay on the expired 0.9.5 ramp, hard for every real install. The escape ends at 1.1.0 and the 1.1.0 migrations record owes this expiry.

sites.mustContain: the census module-name closure over the shipped module list

obligations.reason: 1.0.0 ships tools/modules.json (OWNED — the installer MODULES list finally has a shipped home a consumer gate can read, discharging exports-walls-module-name-validation) and closes every census entry's `module` value against it, so a typo'd module name can no longer park the stale arm permanently dormant while the entry still pre-authorises a ./client barrel. The census is SEEDED, so per the ramp doctrine the closure's findings ship NOTE-only for pre-1.0.0 installs until 1.1.0: a tree that wrote a module name before any list existed to check it against gets one release of dated NOTEs to fix the name or remove the sanction, never a hard red on the update that delivered the list. The register file itself fails closed unramped when absent or malformed — it is owned and arrives with the same release as the check, so its absence is a broken tree, not a consumer choice. The escape ends at 1.1.0 and the 1.1.0 migrations record owes this expiry.

1.0.0 ships tools/support-register.json (the reviewed vendor-support dispositions for the online services and platforms this stack runs on — the decision the deleted e8-eol-closure condition row said someone had to make) and judges it clocklessly in version-sync with a platform-fact closure against the tree's own Postgres/Node pins.
